title: Levels of the Org Chart
description: Walk the management chain from the head of the company down with a recursive CTE.
statement:
The head of the company (no manager) is at **level 1**; the people who report to them are at level 2; their reports are at level 3, and so on.

Return `employee` and `level` for every employee reachable from the head of the company, ordered by `level`, then `employee`. (The company has exactly one employee with no manager.)
starter:
SELECT name AS employee
FROM employees;
variants: INSERT INTO employees VALUES (19, 'Deep One', 1, 18, 1000, '2025-01-01'), (20, 'Deeper Two', 1, 19, 1000, '2025-01-02')
hints: This needs a query that refers to its own result. What is the starting row?
`WITH RECURSIVE chart(id, name, level) AS (anchor UNION ALL step)`. The anchor is the employee with no manager, at level 1.
The step joins `employees` to `chart` on `manager_id = chart.id` and adds 1 to the level.
solution:
WITH RECURSIVE chart(id, name, level) AS (
  SELECT id, name, 1
  FROM employees
  WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.id, e.name, chart.level + 1
  FROM employees AS e
  JOIN chart ON e.manager_id = chart.id
)
SELECT name AS employee, level
FROM chart
ORDER BY level, name;
explanation:
**The idea.** A **recursive CTE** has two parts joined by `UNION ALL`: the *anchor* (here, the head of the company at level 1) and the *recursive step*, which refers to the CTE itself and finds the next row set from the previous one (the people whose manager is someone found in the last round). The database repeats the step, feeding each round's new rows into the next, until a round finds nothing.

**Where it is needed.** Any hierarchy of unknown depth: reporting lines, category trees, threaded comments, bills of materials. A fixed number of self-joins only reaches a fixed depth; the recursive CTE goes as deep as the data.

**Watch for cycles.** If the data loops (A manages B, B manages A) the recursion never ends; real databases limit the depth, and you can carry a path or a depth counter and stop at a maximum.
